content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday blue green deployment work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical blue green deployment tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any blue green deployment bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to blue green deployment (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Validate blue green deployment outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
4. Keep blue green deployment outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Prefer the simplest blue green deployment approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Keep blue green deployment changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. When blue green deployment guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
8. Document any non-obvious blue green deployment decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. State assumptions about blue green deployment explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
10. Surface known limitations of a chosen blue green deployment approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new blue green deployment abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not apply generic blue green deployment advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of blue green deployment correctness.
- Do not skip documenting blue green deployment assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop blue green deployment edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these blue green deployment guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
